title: Ratios, segments & related parties — Coastal Brands
instructions: Coastal Brands, a public company, is preparing its annual report. Use the exhibits to compute ratios, determine reportable segments, and identify the authoritative guidance for a related-party matter.

exhibits.title: Selected financial data
exhibits.content:
| Item | Beginning of year | End of year |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cash | 60,000 | 80,000 |
| Accounts receivable, net | 140,000 | 160,000 |
| Inventory | 210,000 | 250,000 |
| Prepaid expenses | 10,000 | 10,000 |
| Current liabilities | 250,000 | 300,000 |
| Total assets | 1,800,000 | 2,200,000 |
| Total stockholders' equity | 900,000 | 1,100,000 |

Net sales (all on credit): **3,000,000**. Cost of goods sold: **1,840,000**. Net income: **200,000**. No preferred stock.

exhibits.title: Operating segment data ($000s)
exhibits.content:
| Segment | Revenue (external + intersegment) | Profit (loss) | Assets |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Apparel | 1,700 | 260 | 1,000 |
| Footwear | 700 | (120) | 500 |
| Accessories | 250 | 30 | 150 |
| Home goods | 200 | 10 | 250 |
| Online marketplace | 150 | (20) | 100 |

exhibits.title: Email from the controller
exhibits.content: Our CEO's sister owns the logistics firm we used for $400,000 of shipping this year. The draft note says the rates were 'comparable to market,' but we never obtained competing bids.

parts.prompt: Compute these ratios using year-end balances or averages as indicated. Enter ratios to two decimals and days to one decimal (365-day year).

rows.label: Return on equity, as a percentage (average equity)

parts.prompt: Is each operating segment reportable under the 10% quantitative tests?

rows.label: Footwear
rows.explanation: Revenue 700 ≥ 300; also |loss| 120 ≥ 30 (10% of the greater of total profits 300 or total losses 140).

rows.label: Accessories
rows.explanation: Revenue 250 < 300, but profit 30 = 10% of 300 → meets the profit test (and assets 150 < 200 fails).

rows.label: Home goods
rows.explanation: Revenue 200 < 300 and profit 10 < 30, but assets 250 ≥ 200 (10% of 2,000) → meets the asset test.

rows.label: Online marketplace
rows.explanation: Revenue 150 < 300; |loss| 20 < 30; assets 100 < 200 → fails all three 10% tests. (Reportable segments' external revenue must still be checked against the 75% test.)

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) addresses the 'comparable to market' language in the draft related-party note?

excerpts.text: Financial statements disclose material related-party transactions, including the nature of the relationship, a description of the transactions, dollar amounts, and amounts due to or from related parties.

Related-party transactions cannot be presumed to be carried out on an arm's-length basis; representations that they were on terms equivalent to arm's-length transactions are not made unless such representations can be substantiated.
Concentrations are disclosed if they make the entity vulnerable to the risk of a near-term severe impact and it is at least reasonably possible that the events could occur in the near term.
If revenues from a single external customer amount to 10 percent or more of revenues, the entity discloses that fact, the total amount, and the segments reporting the revenues.

parts.explanation: The 'comparable to market' claim is an arm's-length representation. Without competing bids it cannot be substantiated, so it must be removed (850-10-50-5). The other disclosures in 850-10-50-1 are still required.
